definitions.explanation: A wound caused by a sharp object such as a knife, glass, or paper.

examples.japanese: {包丁|ほうちょう}で{指|ゆび}に{切|き}り{傷|きず}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a cut on my finger with a kitchen knife.

examples.japanese: {切|き}り{傷|きず}を{消毒|しょうどく}してバンドエイドを{貼|は}った。
examples.english: I disinfected the cut and put on a bandage.

examples.japanese: {浅|あさ}い{切|き}り{傷|きず}ならすぐに{治|なお}る。
examples.english: A shallow cut will heal quickly.

notes:
A compound of {切|き}り (cutting) + {傷|きず} (wound). Refers specifically to wounds made by sharp objects like knives, glass, or paper.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {切|き}り{傷|きず}を{負|お}う: to sustain a cut
- {切|き}り{傷|きず}を{治療|ちりょう}する: to treat a cut
- {深|ふか}い/{浅|あさ}い{切|き}り{傷|きず}: deep/shallow cut
- {切|き}り{傷|きず}を{消毒|しょうどく}する: to disinfect a cut

OTHER WOUND TYPES:
- {擦|す}り{傷|きず}: scrape, abrasion
- {刺|さ}し{傷|きず}: stab wound
- {打撲傷|だぼくしょう}: bruise, contusion
- やけど: burn
- {噛|か}み{傷|きず}: bite wound

cross_references.label: wound, cut, opening of a wound
